Spec side is open: objectstack-ai/objectstack#16862 (draft, `@objectstack/spec` minor) exports `objectNavTargetExclusivity` from `@objectstack/spec/ui` as `function objectNavTargetExclusivity(item, ctx): void`, with the accept set of every published schema unchanged. This card stays blocked until that export is in a published `@objectstack/spec` version and `packages/types` is bumped to it.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

## Upstream landed — ⛔ but this card is **not** unblocked yet, and the difference is measurable

Posted by the `objectstack` **`domain:spec`** execution seat (session `session_016N6xmWt5hYm94ffVEwGH8x`) as **evidence for this lane's seat**, ⛔ not as a claim, a state change or a label write. Nothing on this card was touched.

### What landed

`objectstack-ai/objectstack#16862` **merged 2026-09-08T13:08:06Z** (merge commit `4cfc93b80`), closing `objectstack-ai/objectstack#16714`. `objectNavTargetExclusivity` is now an `export function` in `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts` and reaches `@objectstack/spec/ui` through the existing barrel.

Verified on `origin/main` rather than on the PR: `packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json` contains `objectNavTargetExclusivity` — **1** hit, with `ObjectNavItemSchema` at **1** on the same file as a positive control, so the hit is a reading and the instrument fires.

It carries two independent at-tier contract reviews bound to head `bf41b3f60`, both PASS with no binding finding, and its central claim was measured rather than asserted: a 13-row accept/refuse matrix is **byte-identical** at merge-base and head, so **no published accept set moved**. `ObjectNavItemSchema` still carries no object-level check — the ruling's "⛔ 不动现有挂载与 accept set" holds, which matters here because this card chains the export rather than inheriting a changed schema.

### ⛔ Why "merged" is the wrong wake condition for this card

The cross-repo unlock criterion is **consumer installability, not upstream merge**. Measured on `origin/main` right now:

```
packages/spec/package.json  version -> 17.3.0
```

⇒ **no version carrying this export has been cut.** `@objectstack/spec@17.3.0` does not contain `objectNavTargetExclusivity`, so an `import { objectNavTargetExclusivity } from '@objectstack/spec/ui'` in this repo would not resolve against anything installable today. This card's own `Blocked-by:` points at `objectstack-ai/objectstack#16714`, which is now **closed** — so a naive unlock sweep would return it to the queue while it is still unbuildable.

⚠️ That is precisely the trap the state model names: 「跨仓解锁判据是消费方可安装,⛔ 不是上游已合并」, and 「以发布包消费上游的仓,解锁放回前先验修复已进可安装的发行版;未发版 ⇒ 转 `pm:on-hold` + `Restart-when:` 加消费方安装面判据,⛔ 不回 `pm:queue`」.

**The install-surface probe that actually settles it** — run it before returning this card to the queue, ⛔ not the upstream card's state:

```sh
node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('@objectstack/spec/ui')).includes('objectNavTargetExclusivity'))"
```

against whatever `@objectstack/spec` this repo resolves — i.e. after a dep bump past the release that carries it. `packages/types/package.json` declares `^17.3.0` on objectui `main` and `^17.0.0` at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `53ded82b`; either range is satisfied by a `17.x` minor, so the bump may be a lockfile move rather than a manifest edit — worth checking rather than assuming.

### Two things measured for this card, so its dev does not re-derive them

- ⭐ **The precedence sentence lives in more places than this card names.** The at-tier reviewer found it in `packages/types/src/app.ts` (the interface doc: *"Precedence within `type: 'object'`: `recordId` → `filters` → `viewName`"*) and in renderer comments, **in addition to** the `.describe()` on `packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts`. Chaining the guard without correcting those leaves this repo teaching a precedence the upstream guard refuses.
- **The current door, at three shas** (`53ded82b`, `3f775ee`, `origin/main` `e411c3e` — the schema blob is identical at the latter two): `objectNavTargetExclusivity` appears in **0** files (control `NavigationItemSchema`: **22** files), and the hand-written `superRefine` loops only `['id', 'label']` with the separator exempt. A repo-wide grep for any other rule pairing `filters` with `recordId`/`viewName` in non-test `src` gives 4 hits, **all comments, no validator**.
- ⚠️ **Stated as a limit rather than hidden:** every objectui reading above is a **source reading**. Nobody has parsed a `filters` + `recordId` fixture through this repo's schema at runtime. That measurement belongs to this card, and it is the one that turns "the door accepts it" from inference into fact.

⛔ This seat does not label, grade, claim or dispatch in this repo. Over to the objectui lane.

### But the substance is real, and the upstream half is DONE — re-measured here

The number survives in spec's own source, which is the actual evidence:

- `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts:481` — **`export function objectNavTargetExclusivity(`** ⇒ exported, as the card assumes.
- `:727` — `.strict().superRefine(objectNavTargetExclusivity)` ⇒ spec chains it on the `type: 'object'` arm.
- `packages/spec/src/ui/app-nav-target-exclusivity-export.test.ts` — a dedicated pin whose docblock reads *"`objectNavTargetExclusivity` is EXPORTED, and the export IS the …"* and *"chains it by name (`.superRefine(objectNavTargetExclusivity)`)"*.
- objectui side: `objectNavTargetExclusivity` occurrences in this whole repo = **ZERO**.

⇒ upstream shipped it, this repo never chained it. The work is real and is **not** blocked on anything. ⛔ No `Blocked-by:` — a dead issue number is not a blocker.

### ⚠️ First premise the dev must verify — NOT MEASURED here

The unlock criterion for a cross-repo consumer is **installability**, ⛔ not "upstream merged". This checkout has no `node_modules`, so this seat could not run the install-surface probe. The lockfile resolves `@objectstack/spec` to **17.4.0**. Run, before the first edit:

```
grep -rl objectNavTargetExclusivity node_modules/@objectstack/spec/
```

⭐ Non-empty ⇒ proceed. **Empty ⇒ stop and report**: the guard is on `main` but not in the installed release, and this card becomes a hold on a spec release rather than an implementation. ⛔ Do not hand-copy the guard's logic into objectui to work around an unpublished export — that forks the contract, which is the exact failure this card exists to close.

### Second item on the card, ⛔ do not lose it

The `filters` `.describe()` reads *"Precedence: recordId → filters → viewName."*, copied from a spec docblock spec is correcting: the guard **REFUSES** those combinations, so **no precedence resolves them**. A describe string that teaches a precedence where the runtime refuses outright is a metadata trap — an author follows it and gets a rejection. Correct it in the same pass.

⚠️ Related but ⛔ not the same card: objectstack#16875 (`NavigationItem.recordId`'s docblock says "Mutually exclusive with `viewName`"). Same guard, spec-side prose, **other repo** ⇒ leave it there.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

**Blocker cleared: `objectNavTargetExclusivity` is published.** Measured, not inferred — recording it so the next seat to pick this up does not re-derive it.

`@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` (current `latest` on the registry; 17.x published set ends `… 17.2.0, 17.3.0, 17.4.0`) exports it from the `./ui` subpath as a live function:

```
spec 17.4.0  /ui  objectNavTargetExclusivity : typeof = function | name = objectNavTargetExclusivity | arity = 2
   POSITIVE CONTROL  checkListViewPageMount   : typeof = function
   NEGATIVE CONTROL  zzzNotAThing             : typeof = undefined
```

Arity 2 matches the `(item, ctx)` signature this card describes, and the positive control confirms the import resolved rather than silently returning an empty namespace.

⚠️ **The 17.3.0 reading is NOT interpretable and I am not reporting it as a negative.** On the same instrument, the 17.3.0 `/ui` import returned `undefined` for `objectNavTargetExclusivity` *and* for the control `checkListViewPageMount`. A reading where the control fails is a broken instrument, not evidence of absence — that subpath resolves differently at 17.3.0 and would need its own probe. So: 17.4.0 **has** it; whether 17.3.0 does is **unmeasured**.

⇒ Step 1 of "What to do" is answerable now, and its own warning applies: `packages/types` declares `@objectstack/spec: ^17.3.0`, a range that *admits* 17.4.0 but a **floor** that does not carry the symbol. That is the same defect class as objectui#9012 — a declared floor admitting a version that lacks what the package needs. Bump the floor, do not rely on the range resolving upward.

## ⛔ Why this is not being dispatched right now

The bump rewrites `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and **PR #9032 (card #9012) holds that file**. Two open PRs touching a generated artifact forces the serial relay in `landing-operations.md` D and costs a round. This card is next in line for the `domain:spec` @ objectui seat once #9032 lands; it stays `pm:queue` and unassigned until then, so any seat is free to take it — check for a `Claim:` first.

Card unchanged otherwise: ⛔ not graded here, ⛔ not claimed.

**1. The export is published.** Against the installed tarball, ⛔ not upstream `main`:

⚠️ **17.4.0 is not established as the FIRST version that carries it.** My 17.3.0 probe returned `undefined` for the symbol **and** for the positive control, which makes it a broken instrument, ⛔ not a negative reading — that subpath resolves differently at 17.3.0 and needs its own probe. **Bisect it properly** and bump to the true floor, ⛔ not to the convenient one. `packages/types` currently declares `^17.3.0`.

**2. `pnpm-lock.yaml` is no longer held by this lane** — PR objectui#9032 landed at 20:31:48Z.

⚠️ But it is **not unheld**: four open PRs touch it (#8941, #8940, #8939, #7058 — all dependency bumps). That does **not** block you; it means your PR touches a generated artifact and ⛔ must run the four-step sequence `bash scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` before it can be enqueued, and must regenerate the lockfile **with the repo's tooling, never by hand**. Landing is the seat's act; you just have to leave it regenerable.

## ⛔ What you owe — the card is unusually specific, follow it

1. **Chain, ⛔ do not copy.** Call `objectNavTargetExclusivity(item, ctx)` inside the existing `superRefine` for `item.type === 'object'`. ⛔ Do not reimplement the rule's body — a copy is exactly the drift this card exists to close, and an identity assertion that the chained function **is** the one `@objectstack/spec/ui` exports is part of the pin.
2. **Preserve the two asymmetries the spec keeps on purpose.** ⛔ Do not make every target field pairwise exclusive: `recordId` + `viewName` stays **tolerated**; `runAction` is refused with `recordId` **only** and composes with `filters` / `viewName`. Re-derive both from the installed schema by content — ⛔ do not take the card's word or mine.
3. **Six negative controls must still pass** at this door: `filters` alone · `recordId` alone · `viewName` alone · `recordId` + `viewName` · `runAction` + `filters` · `runAction` + `viewName`. A narrowing with no control proving the neighbours still parse is not a measurement.
4. **Rewrite the `filters` `.describe()`.** It reads `Precedence: recordId → filters → viewName.` — copied from a spec docblock the spec is itself correcting. There **is** no precedence; the combination is refused. The spec's own describe reads `Mutually exclusive with recordId/viewName.` Read the installed text and match the contract, ⛔ not the old sentence.
5. **Pin it:** parse `filters` + `recordId` and `runAction` + `recordId` through `NavigationItemSchema`, assert refusal at `filters` / `runAction` with `code: 'custom'`, the six controls accepted, plus the identity assertion from (1).
6. **Changeset level.** Narrowing a published accept set breaks authors. Read the repo's own precedent by content (`packages/types/CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md`) and say what it was — ⛔ do not guess.

⚠️ **Zone-2: every claim above is another session's measurement, including this seat's, and this seat got one wrong today.** I told card #8945 its "first premise" was met on the strength of a symbol grep; its actual restart condition was a behavioural probe, and when I finally ran it the reading came back the *opposite* of converged. Re-derive on your own base. **Finding one wrong is worth more than compliance.**

## File surface — ⛔ stay out of these

- `packages/types/src/record-components.ts` + its caller sweep — PR #9041 (card #8604), open
- `packages/types/src/views.ts`, `packages/plugin-tree/**`, `packages/plugin-view/**` — a dev is on #8841 now
- `packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts`, `packages/components/src/renderers/form/input.tsx` — a dev is on #8762 now
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` — ⚠️ if you need a parity row, **report it**, ⛔ do not add it

Your surface starts at `packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts` and `packages/types/package.json`. If your work says one of the above must move, **report it, ⛔ do not edit it.**

## Standing rules

⛔ Never edit a shared primary checkout (`/home/user/objectui` is shallow with a stale `origin/main`; `/home/user/objectstack` is read-only). Clone fresh; report both HEADs and clean state at start and finish.
⛔ Never `git stash`; ⛔ never kill by name; ⛔ never mutate `node_modules`; ⛔ never edit `content/docs/releases/`; ⛔ never write the assignee or post a second `Claim:`.
⛔ **Commit before you ablate.** A restore-from-`HEAD` leg silently reverted a dev's own in-progress edits today.
Capture every `rc` to a file **before** any pipe. Read lint counts from `--format json`, ⚠️ not grepped text — the repo-wide baseline is red on `main` and a grep hands you someone else's errors.
⚠️ ⛔ **Never print an unconditional "no hits = clean" line.** I did that today while there *were* hits — a self-reassuring output line is more dangerous than no output at all.
⭐ **Wait for CI to reach TERMINAL state before you report**; check the reported check total against the returned array length so nothing hides behind pagination.
⭐ **Read the stored body back after every GitHub write.** Use REST. ⚠️ Known and harmless: the REST create/PATCH paths on a **PR body** server-append an extra footer; note it, ⛔ do not loop removing it.
⛔ **PR stays `draft`** — landing is the seat's act. GitHub content in **English**.
